title: Lua: Fix handling of Wireshark exceptions inside dissectors
description:
The Wireshark kazlib portable exception handling and Lua's
exception handling when compiled for C both use setjmp() and
longjmp(). dissect_lua and heur_dissect_lua are always called
within a Wireshark TRY block, and the dissectors they call might
encounter Wireshark exceptions.

The Lua functions needs to be called in a protected manner in
order to deal with Lua errors without aborting the program.
However, Wireshark exceptions can cause a jump out of the cleanup
routines that remove the number of C functions from the Lua stack,
and remove entries from the chain of longjmp destinations. If
lua_error is subsequently called, that causes a longjmp to a
no longer valid address, undefined behavior that is usually a crash.
Even if lua_error is not called, never decrementing the number of
C functions supposedly on the stack (but actually exited due to
the longjmp) eventually causes our Lua state to cease functioning
and just return errors about "C stack overflow."

Deal with this by, in dissect_lua and heur_dissect_lua, creating
a throwaway new Lua "thread" and remove it from the stack for
garbage collection at the end of the function. That ensures that
not just our lua_State's Lua stack, but also its count of C functions
doesn't grow from frame to frame. It also means that we can report
Lua tracebacks for any Wireshark exception encountered in a
Lua dissector called from these functions.

Undo a bit of the fix for #18681 because we don't want to catch
non fatal errors there after all.

Handling Wireshark exceptions is necessary for #15655, but there'
more to be done.

Fix #13674.
